skills.name: Precise Action Parameter Execution
skills.description: The agent completes the right type of action but uses incorrect arguments—wrong item IDs, wrong payment methods, wrong flight combinations, or wrong reservation targets—resulting in a DB state that differs from what was requested. The agent appears to confirm the correct plan but then submits tool calls with subtly wrong values.
skills.reasoning: Across both domains, the agent consistently calls the correct tool type but submits wrong item/flight/payment identifiers, indicating failure to accurately map confirmed choices back to tool call arguments.

skills.name: Full Scope Completion for Bulk Operations
skills.description: When the user requests the same action across multiple records (all reservations, all pending orders, every item matching a criterion), the agent processes only a subset—typically the first one found—without applying the operation to the remaining in-scope records. The agent terminates prematurely instead of iterating through all qualifying entities.
skills.reasoning: The agent retrieves one record, acts on it, and reports success without checking whether the same operation applies to other records the user specified or which meet the stated filter criteria.

skills.name: Numerical Calculation Accuracy
skills.description: The agent makes arithmetic errors when computing totals, refund amounts, price differences, or savings figures—either by calling the calculate tool with the wrong expression, misreading line items, or reporting a number that was never derived from the actual data. Critical numeric values required by the task are either wrong or never produced.
skills.reasoning: Both domains show repeated failures where the agent states or omits specific numeric values (refund amounts, cost deltas, totals) that are required to be correct and communicated, indicating poor arithmetic planning.

skills.name: Policy Boundary Maintenance Under Pressure
skills.description: When a user applies social pressure, flattery, emotional framing, or repeated insistence, the agent grants exceptions that exceed what policy permits—issuing certificates larger than allowed, processing refunds to non-original payment methods, or abandoning valid refusals. The agent conflates empathy with compliance.
skills.reasoning: In both domains, agents consistently drift from policy-compliant responses when users apply emotional or persistent pressure, issuing incorrect amounts or taking disallowed actions rather than holding the policy boundary.

skills.name: Exhaustive Record Discovery
skills.description: The agent fails to locate all relevant records before acting—stopping at the first matching order, only fetching some of a user's reservations, or missing orders at different addresses. When a user makes a broad request ('all my orders', 'any upcoming flights'), the agent acts on an incomplete picture of the account.
skills.reasoning: Tasks requiring the agent to survey the full account state before acting expose a consistent failure to iterate through all records, leading to missed operations on records that were never fetched.

skills.name: Proactive Required Information Communication
skills.description: The agent completes a transaction but fails to proactively state specific numeric or factual values that the task requires to be communicated—such as exact refund totals, savings amounts, tracking numbers, or product counts—even when these values are available from tool results already in context.
skills.reasoning: Communicate check failures across both domains cluster around the same pattern: the agent executes the action correctly but omits stating a precise value the evaluator required, showing it does not reliably surface all task-critical data to the user.

skills.name: Precise Parameter Fidelity
skills.description: The agent selects the correct high-level action but populates it with wrong parameters — wrong item IDs, wrong amounts, wrong flight numbers, or wrong payment targets — even when the correct values are present in tool results. This differs from ignoring a step entirely: the action fires, but with incorrect arguments.
skills.reasoning: Across both domains the agent consistently performs the right category of action but with wrong specifics drawn from tool output — wrong flight HAT numbers in airline changes, wrong desk-lamp item IDs in retail exchanges, and wrong certificate amounts — indicating a persistent gap in accurately reading and propagating values from retrieved data into tool arguments.

skills.name: Exhaustive Multi-Target Execution
skills.description: When a user requests the same operation across multiple entities (all reservations, all pending orders, all items), the agent addresses only a subset and treats the task as complete, failing to iterate over every applicable target.
skills.reasoning: In A18 the agent downgrades one of five reservations and stops; in R54 it retrieves six orders but cancels only two; the pattern is consistent — bulk 'apply-to-all' requests are partially satisfied because the agent treats the first match as completion rather than iterating to cover every qualifying target.

skills.name: Conditional Fallback Reasoning
skills.description: When a user specifies a priority-ordered or conditional chain of preferences ('do X; if not possible, do Y; if Y fails, do Z'), the agent either collapses to the first option, skips the decision tree, or executes the wrong branch without evaluating the precondition.
skills.reasoning: R57 requires checking gift-card availability before deciding whether to cancel, and A19 requires preferring later-same-day over next-day flights; in both cases the agent executes without evaluating the stated condition, revealing an inability to track and branch on multi-clause user constraints.

skills.name: Constraint-Aware Transfer Escalation
skills.description: The agent must recognize when a user's stated goal violates a hard system constraint (e.g., refund must go to original payment method, reservation origin/destination cannot change) and proactively escalate to a human agent rather than either refusing repeatedly or silently executing the wrong action.
skills.reasoning: R10 and R12 involve users requesting cross-order payment routing that the system explicitly rejects; A13 involves a destination change the system cannot process; in all cases the agent either repeats refusals without escalating or incorrectly completes the transaction with the original payment method, showing it cannot map 'repeated impossible request' to the escalation action.

skills.name: Exact Numerical Communication
skills.description: After performing calculations or retrieving balances, the agent must communicate the precise numerical result (total savings, refund amount, balance remaining) to the user before or after acting; failures occur when the agent states an approximate or omitted figure rather than the exact value derived from data.
skills.reasoning: Communicate-check failures consistently cite specific dollar amounts (e.g., '23553', '918.43', '44.08') that are verifiable from tool results but absent from the agent's reply — the agent narrates the action without completing the required numerical disclosure, which is a distinct failure from the calculation itself being wrong.

skills.name: Scope Resolution from Ambiguous References
skills.description: When users reference entities without explicit identifiers ('my last order', 'the other reservation', 'the office stuff'), the agent must resolve the reference against retrieved data to find the correct target; failures result in acting on the wrong item, skipping the lookup, or requesting redundant clarification.
skills.reasoning: A21 requires identifying which of seven reservations is the IAH-DEN round trip; R33 requires knowing which order contains 'office items'; in both domains the agent either retrieves all data but acts on the first match, misidentifies the target, or asks for identifiers the user already provided indirectly — all manifestations of failed reference resolution.

skills.name: Constraint-Faithful Item Selection
skills.description: When searching for a replacement item, the agent fails to match the user's specific attribute constraints (e.g., compatibility, power source, size preferences), instead selecting the first available item that partially matches. It also fails to respect conditional preference orderings like 'prefer X, then Y, then Z'.
skills.reasoning: In R1 the agent confused Google Home with Google Assistant; in R5-9 it ignored power-source preference orderings; in A13/A15/A16 it selected wrong destination or cabin class — all share the same root cause of not faithfully enforcing user-stated attribute constraints when choosing among tool-returned variants.

skills.name: Policy-Compliant Action Execution
skills.description: The agent executes actions that violate system rules (e.g., changing non-changeable ticket types, refunding to non-original payment methods, issuing compensation for ineligible events), either by ignoring explicit policy constraints or by failing to verify eligibility before acting.
skills.reasoning: A31/A36 changed basic-economy flights (not permitted); A38/A49 issued unsolicited certificates; A39 issued certificates the user never requested; R10/R12/R82/R83 refunded to a payment method other than the original — all are violations of stated operational rules the agent had access to but did not apply.

skills.name: Multi-Step Operation Sequencing
skills.description: When a task requires multiple dependent operations (e.g., return an item then exchange, modify then cancel, look up then update across multiple orders), the agent sequences them in the wrong order, applies the wrong operation type for the current order state, or fails to complete all required steps.
skills.reasoning: R19/R27 attempted exchange after initiating a return (invalidating the order state); R36/R65 tried to return or modify delivered/non-pending orders; A22/A24 failed passenger-count matching; A37/A44 required sequenced cancel+upgrade+cancel — all share the failure to track state across sequential operations and apply the correct tool for the current state.

skills.name: Payment and Calculation Accuracy
skills.description: The agent makes arithmetic errors when computing totals for multi-item or multi-passenger transactions, or incorrectly attributes which payment instrument should be charged or credited, leading to tool errors or incorrect financial outcomes.
skills.reasoning: A20/A25/A42 produced payment-amount mismatch errors; A17 overestimated gift card balance; R36/R37 miscounted items when attempting cancellation; A2/A8/A10/A12 booked with wrong passenger counts or seat pricing — all stem from failure to correctly track and compute financial totals across items, passengers, or payment splits.

skills.name: Boundary Holding Under User Pressure
skills.description: When users claim entitlements beyond what the data supports, express strong dissatisfaction, or insist on policy exceptions, the agent incorrectly concedes by offering unauthorized compensation, accepting unverified claims, or transferring to a human rather than clearly communicating the correct outcome.
skills.reasoning: A27 gave full refund to a complaining user whose situation did not meet cancellation policy; A38 issued $150 to a user who falsely claimed 3 passengers; R47/R83 transferred to human instead of firmly stating the correct policy — the shared pattern is capitulating to pressure rather than accurately applying the rules.

skills.name: Proactive Required Information Communication
skills.description: The agent completes the database action correctly but omits specific details the user explicitly asked for or that are required by the task specification (e.g., tracking numbers, material specifications, exact price differences), causing a communication-score failure despite a correct database state.
skills.reasoning: R103 performed all returns and modifications correctly but omitted the tracking number the user asked for; R24 correctly identified t-shirts but omitted the polyester material detail; A11 completed the downgrade but failed to state the correct refund amount upfront — all share the pattern of correct action with incomplete information disclosure.

skills.name: Policy Boundary Enforcement
skills.description: The agent fails to hold firm to eligibility rules when processing requests: it approves cancellations, refunds, or modifications that do not meet stated preconditions, especially when users apply emotional pressure, make false claims, or express frustration. This includes acting on unverified user assertions (e.g., claimed insurance, claimed flight status) and yielding to urgency instead of checking whether the action is actually permitted.
skills.reasoning: Across both domains the agent executes actions that violate clearly stated eligibility criteria, either because it trusts user claims without verification or because it capitulates to emotional or persistent pressure rather than applying the rule consistently.

skills.name: Precise Attribute Matching Under Preferences
skills.description: When a user specifies multiple constraints on a target item or option (e.g., color, size, capacity, CPU, water-resistance, power source preference order), the agent selects a variant that satisfies only some of those constraints or picks the wrong item entirely. The agent also sometimes executes the correct action type (exchange vs. return vs. modify) on the wrong item.
skills.reasoning: In both domains the agent consistently loses track of one or more user-specified attribute constraints when choosing among multiple options, producing outcomes that technically resemble what was asked but differ in a critical dimension the user had specified.

skills.name: Multi-step Conditional Branch Tracking
skills.description: When a user specifies a conditional action plan ('if X, do Y; otherwise do Z') or chains multiple dependent operations across several turns, the agent fails to correctly maintain and execute the correct branch. It either flattens all conditions into the first branch, forgets a later branch, or executes operations in the wrong order that invalidates subsequent steps.
skills.reasoning: Across airline (multi-reservation filter-then-act flows) and retail (conditional exchange/return/cancel chains), the agent loses track of the conditional structure the user established, executing the wrong branch or missing a necessary step after a tool call changes the state.

skills.name: Numerical Calculation and Disclosure
skills.description: The agent produces or omits incorrect numerical totals that it is required to communicate: total refund amounts, total savings, remaining balances, specific charges to individual payment methods, or counts of available items. These errors occur both when amounts need to be summed across multiple records and when a single price difference is computed.
skills.reasoning: In both airline (aggregate savings, per-card charges, compensation amounts) and retail (total refund across orders, price differences, available variant counts), the agent either computes the wrong figure or fails to disclose the value the evaluation requires.

skills.name: Cross-Record Information Retrieval
skills.description: When fulfilling a request requires information that exists in a different record than the one the user mentions (e.g., an address stored in another order, a delayed flight reservation the user does not specify by ID, or finding which order contains a particular item), the agent does not proactively search across all user records and instead either fails to locate the needed data or uses the wrong record as its reference.
skills.reasoning: Across both domains, when the answer to 'which record' or 'what address/flight' is implicit rather than stated, the agent fails to enumerate and inspect all user records to find the right one, leading to acting on the wrong record or abandoning the task.

skills.name: Graceful Partial Failure Recovery
skills.description: When one step in a multi-step request encounters a hard block (unsupported refund method, undelivered item, wrong order ID, no matching item), the agent escalates to a human transfer or abandons remaining achievable sub-tasks rather than completing the parts it can and clearly explaining the constraint on the blocked part.
skills.reasoning: In retail scenarios where a single sub-request fails, the agent treats the failure as terminal and transfers or stops rather than completing the remaining valid sub-requests and communicating what it could not do and why.

skills.name: Multi-attribute Item Selection
skills.description: When a user specifies multiple ranked or conjunctive attributes for a replacement item (e.g., size AND color AND material, or 'battery first, then USB'), the agent must correctly identify the single best matching variant from the product catalog, not just one that satisfies some attributes. The agent fails when it picks a variant that satisfies only a subset of constraints, picks the wrong item from a filtered set, or conflates which item in an order the user is referring to.
skills.reasoning: In both airline (wrong flight/cabin combination booked) and retail (wrong product variant exchanged despite correct product type), the agent selects an item that does not match all user-specified attributes when multiple must be satisfied simultaneously.

skills.name: Policy Constraint Enforcement
skills.description: The agent must check and respect hard constraints before executing irreversible actions: refunds must go to the original payment method, compensation amounts must follow policy rules, cancellations require specific eligibility conditions, and unauthorized payment methods must be rejected. The agent fails when it executes the action anyway after a constraint-violating request, ignores the error returned by the system, or misidentifies which constraint applies.
skills.reasoning: In airline tasks the agent issues certificates of wrong amounts or cancels ineligible reservations; in retail tasks the agent accepts refund targets that differ from the original payment method, even when the system returns an error.

skills.name: Action Scope Precision
skills.description: When a multi-step task involves several sub-actions (e.g., change flight AND add baggage, cancel item A AND keep item B, update address AND update items), the agent must execute exactly the right set of sub-actions on exactly the right target objects. The agent fails when it applies changes to the wrong order or reservation, omits required sub-actions, applies modifications that were not requested, or conflates targets across multiple orders.
skills.reasoning: Across both domains the agent consistently either does too much (applying changes to the full reservation when only the return leg was requested) or too little (updating items but not the address, or canceling the wrong order) when tasks contain multiple parallel or sequential sub-goals.

skills.name: Ranked Fallback Resolution
skills.description: When the user expresses a preference ordering such as 'option A if available, otherwise B, otherwise C' or 'if cost exceeds X do Y instead', the agent must correctly resolve the chain at execution time by checking availability/conditions sequentially and acting on the correct fallback, not on the first option stated regardless of feasibility.
skills.reasoning: In airline tasks the agent books wrong payment splits or ignores budget cutoffs; in retail tasks it picks the wrong item from a ranked preference list (e.g., battery > USB > AC) by not checking availability before committing to the top preference.

skills.name: Correct Target Identification
skills.description: When a user references a target (order, reservation, item) without a unique ID, or when multiple similar candidates exist, the agent must search for and confirm the correct one before acting. The agent fails when it retrieves the wrong order among a user's multiple orders, acts on a reservation not matching the described route or date, or confuses items across different orders when the user's description is ambiguous.
skills.reasoning: In airline tasks the agent cancels the wrong reservation or fails to retrieve the correct one from multiple reservations; in retail tasks it finds the wrong order or operates on a different order's items when the user described an item without specifying the order ID.

skills.name: State-Aware Operation Sequencing
skills.description: Before executing certain operations (exchanges, returns, cancellations, modifications), the agent must check the current state of the target object (e.g., pending vs. delivered, already returned, already modified) and apply the correct operation type that is valid for that state. The agent fails when it attempts to return a pending order, exchange a delivered-and-already-returned item, or use an exchange API on a pending order that requires a modify API.
skills.reasoning: In both domains the agent calls the wrong operation for the item's current lifecycle state—using 'exchange' on a pending order, 'return' on a not-yet-delivered order, or acting after a state change has already rendered the intended operation invalid.

skills.name: Payment Split Arithmetic
skills.description: When a payment is split across multiple instruments (e.g., gift card + credit card), the agent must compute each instrument's contribution so that the amounts exactly sum to the total price. The agent consistently miscalculates the split, submitting a wrong per-instrument amount and triggering payment mismatch errors.
skills.reasoning: All five failures share the same root cause: the agent calls a booking or update tool with payment_amounts that do not sum to the declared total price, causing repeated 'Payment amount does not add up' errors even after retry attempts.

skills.name: Order-Status Gating for Mutations
skills.description: Each mutation operation (exchange, return, modify) is only valid for items in specific lifecycle states (delivered, pending, etc.). The agent must check the current status before selecting a tool and must not apply a delivered-item API to a non-delivered item or a pending-item API to a processed item.
skills.reasoning: In every case the agent calls exchange_delivered_order_items on an order whose status had already changed (return requested, non-delivered) or modify_pending_order_items on a non-pending order, producing 'Non-delivered order cannot be exchanged' or 'Non-pending order cannot be modified' errors.

skills.name: Collection Size Invariant in Updates
skills.description: When updating a collection (passenger list, item list) the API requires the new collection to preserve the original size unless the operation explicitly supports deletion. The agent must supply the full retained set rather than only the items being added or removed.
skills.reasoning: All four failures stem from the agent submitting a passenger or item list that is shorter than the original without understanding the constraint, yielding 'Number of passengers does not match' or 'The number of items to be exchanged should match' errors.

skills.name: Action Fidelity Under Pressure
skills.description: When a user complains, pressures, or fabricates a grievance, the agent must act only on what is verified in the system and only on what was actually requested. The agent should not perform unsolicited high-impact actions (cancellations, certificate issuance) to placate the user or resolve a situation it cannot verify.
skills.reasoning: In these cases the agent either cancelled a reservation not requested, issued a travel certificate for a delay that the system showed as 'available', cancelled an entire order when the user only asked about payment splitting, or indefinitely indulged off-topic conversation instead of completing the task.

skills.name: Complete Multi-Step Request Execution
skills.description: When a user requests several independent sub-tasks in one conversation turn, the agent must execute every sub-task before concluding. A common failure is correctly completing one action while silently omitting another (e.g., changing a flight leg but dropping the return leg, or updating an item but forgetting the address change).
skills.reasoning: In all these cases the agent successfully calls the tool for one part of the request but never issues the tool call for the other part, resulting in a correct COMMUNICATE score but a failed DB score because the full desired state was never reached.

skills.name: Identity Resolution with Fallback
skills.description: When a primary identity lookup (name+zip, email) fails, the agent must systematically try alternative identifiers or ask the user to clarify, rather than repeatedly retrying the same failed query or immediately giving up. Failing to resolve the user identity blocks all downstream actions.
skills.reasoning: In each failure the agent either loops on the same wrong lookup parameters, attempts a nonsensical ID, or escalates to a human agent prematurely without exhausting available alternatives (e.g., switching between name+zip and email lookups).

skills.name: Exact Parameter Recall
skills.description: When executing tool calls, the agent consistently selects wrong specific identifiers or values — wrong item IDs, flight numbers, payment method IDs, reservation IDs, refund amounts, or order IDs — even though the correct information is present in the conversation context. The right action type is chosen but the specific arguments are incorrect.
skills.reasoning: This is the single most common failure pattern: the agent performs the semantically correct action (update flight, exchange item, cancel reservation) but with wrong specific parameter values, causing the database operation to act on the wrong entity or with incorrect attributes.

skills.name: Sequential Multi-step Completion
skills.description: When a task requires executing multiple distinct operations in sequence, the agent fails to complete all of them — either stopping after the first operation, missing secondary requests, or having later steps become blocked because an earlier action changed the state in a way that prevents subsequent operations (e.g., initiating a return before attempting an exchange on the same order).
skills.reasoning: The agent systematically fails at compound tasks: it either does some but not all requested operations, or the ordering of operations creates state conflicts (e.g., return-then-exchange) that the agent fails to anticipate or work around.

skills.name: Policy-Constrained Action Selection
skills.description: The agent misapplies domain policies when choosing what action to take: it either refuses valid requests by citing an inapplicable policy constraint, performs actions that should be blocked by policy, or takes the wrong conditional branch in tasks with if-then-else logic (e.g., 'cancel if unavailable, otherwise modify').
skills.reasoning: The agent consistently makes the wrong binary choice when policies constrain action eligibility — sometimes completing actions that should be refused or transferred, and other times refusing or transferring when the action should be completed.

skills.name: Task Scope Adherence
skills.description: The agent either over-executes (cancels an entire order when asked to cancel one item, issues a large compensation when a small one was specified, operates on adjacent resources not mentioned in the task) or under-executes by narrowing the task scope and missing required work. This is about the breadth of WHAT actions are taken, not the specifics of HOW they are parameterized.
skills.reasoning: The agent systematically misjudges the intended scope: it cancels whole orders when partial actions were needed, issues disproportionate compensations, or applies exchanges to the wrong item category — showing consistent difficulty calibrating how much to act versus how much to withhold.

skills.name: Conversation Closure Under Social Pressure
skills.description: Once the task is functionally complete, the agent fails to close the conversation when the user engages in flattery, emotional storytelling, or sustained indecision. The agent keeps responding in kind — sometimes taking additional unintended actions — rather than politely acknowledging and ending the interaction.
skills.reasoning: The agent lacks a termination signal when customers become socially or emotionally engaging after task completion: it gets drawn into multi-turn flattery loops (A9: 30+ turns), prolonged narrative engagement (R80: t-shirt decision loop), or off-topic tool calls (R62: random product lookups after declining irrelevant poem question).

skills.name: Tool Error Recovery
skills.description: When a tool call returns an error, the agent enters repetitive retry loops, invents workaround actions that compound the error state, or fails to reach a clean resolution within the conversation step limit. The agent does not cleanly detect and communicate an impasse, nor does it fall back to a transfer-to-human path when recovery is impossible.
skills.reasoning: These cases all hit max_steps or too_many_errors termination because the agent loops on failed tool calls: it retries the same failing call, generates alternative workarounds that create new errors, or calls irrelevant tools while unable to progress — never recognizing that the impasse requires escalation or graceful termination.

skills.name: Policy Compliance Under Pressure
skills.description: The agent incorrectly approves requests that violate eligibility rules, often capitulating when users apply emotional pressure, false claims, or repeated insistence. Passed tasks show the agent correctly refusing or transferring; failed tasks show it granting refunds, cancellations, or compensation that policy forbids.
skills.reasoning: In A26/A39/A41/A43 the agent cancelled basic-economy or multi-passenger reservations that did not meet cancellation criteria; in A47/A49 it cancelled flights despite insurance not covering the stated reason; in R46/R47 it promised an impossible 3-day refund timeline; in R82/R83 it attempted to refund to a non-original payment method — all cases where user pushback caused the agent to abandon correct policy enforcement.

skills.name: Precise Constraint-Aware Resource Selection
skills.description: The agent selects the wrong flight, product variant, or order item when multiple candidates exist and the task specifies constraints such as cheapest price, specific attributes, airport flexibility, or matching an existing record. Passed tasks involve simpler or more explicit selection; failed tasks require filtering a search space against several simultaneous criteria.
skills.reasoning: A15/A16 chose incorrect flight combinations when given open airport options; A20 booked a departure that violated the stated time constraint; R52 picked the wrong camera zoom variant; R93 used the wrong order entirely — all cases where the agent browsed available options but matched the wrong one against the user's stated requirements.

skills.name: Multi-Step Transaction Execution
skills.description: The agent fails to complete all required sub-operations when a task involves a coordinated sequence of distinct actions (e.g., cancel-then-rebook, return-then-exchange, or address-change plus item-modification). Passed tasks involving single actions succeed; failed tasks require the agent to plan, execute, and verify multiple dependent or independent steps without omitting any.
skills.reasoning: A14 required cancel+rebook with per-reservation certificate limits; A23 required three separate bookings to use three certificates; R41/R42 modified the item but omitted the required order address change; R19 broke after the first return because it did not complete the subsequent exchange — in every case the agent completed some steps while missing others that were equally required.

skills.name: Scope Discipline Under Distraction
skills.description: The agent abandons or derails its primary task when users introduce emotional narratives, flattery, unrelated questions, or side complaints. Passed tasks involve users who stay on topic; failed tasks include users who deliberately shift the conversation away from the original request before it is completed.
skills.reasoning: In A2 the user's delay complaint redirected the agent into issuing a goodwill certificate instead of completing the flight booking; in A9 repeated compliments caused the agent to lose track of the three-reservation task; in R62 a nonsensical poem question caused the agent to execute a spurious order modification — each failure shares the pattern of the user successfully steering the agent away from the assigned goal.

skills.name: Action Execution Verification
skills.description: The agent reports task completion without having called the required write-side tool, or abandons an achievable task when a single sub-step fails rather than finding an alternative path. Passed tasks show actual tool invocations confirming the state change; failed tasks contain either phantom confirmations with no corresponding tool call or premature escalation/transfer when continuation was still possible.
skills.reasoning: A18 calculated the savings and announced the downgrade was complete without ever calling update_reservation_flights; R7/R9 confirmed the exchange plan verbally but never called exchange_delivered_order_items; R106 transferred to a human after one failed lookup method without trying the alternative — all share the agent treating intermediate reasoning or partial progress as a completed outcome.

skills.name: Multi-Constraint Logical Reasoning
skills.description: The agent cannot construct or verify a solution that must simultaneously satisfy several independent constraints such as price ceilings, payment-method restrictions, attribute requirements, and policy eligibility — particularly when the constraints interact or require comparing multiple candidates.
skills.reasoning: A14 required finding the cheapest business round-trip while using at most one certificate per reservation across three new bookings; R36/R37 required resolving a payment-shortage constraint (insufficient card balance) with a creative split or item removal; R59 required conditionally cancelling the older of two pending orders based on placement date — in each case the agent found a partial solution that violated at least one stated constraint.

skills.name: Multi-Attribute Constraint Satisfaction
skills.description: When selecting an item or option that must simultaneously match multiple criteria, the agent chooses an option satisfying some but not all constraints, or fails to recognize when no valid option exists.
skills.reasoning: Failures occur in both retail (wrong item variant selected) and airline (wrong flight option chosen) when the agent matches partial attribute sets instead of verifying all constraints hold together.

skills.name: Conditional Branch Execution
skills.description: When user instructions contain explicit if/then contingencies or the user revises scope at a confirmation checkpoint, the agent proceeds with the default action instead of following the conditional branch.
skills.reasoning: Both domains show systematic failure when user instructions embed if/then logic; the agent defaults to the most direct action path regardless of branching conditions that should alter scope or method.

skills.name: Exhaustive Scope Coverage
skills.description: When a task requires applying an action to all matching entities across multiple orders, items, or reservations, the agent applies it to a subset and then terminates without checking remaining entities.
skills.reasoning: The agent completes the first few matching operations and declares success in both retail (missing orders with qualifying items) and airline (only cancelling some of many reservations).

skills.name: Proactive Numerical Communication
skills.description: When a user explicitly asks for a computed total, count, or specific fact, the agent either skips the calculation, computes an incorrect value, or omits the number from its response despite being asked.
skills.reasoning: Across both domains, tasks that explicitly request a specific computed value reveal the agent consistently skipping the calculate step or failing to surface the result in its reply.

skills.name: Implicit Reference Resolution
skills.description: When a user refers to information stored in their account or another context without explicitly stating it, the agent either prompts the user to reveal it directly or retrieves the value from the wrong source.
skills.reasoning: Tasks where users say 'look it up in my orders or profile' expose the agent's failure to autonomously locate and use the correct stored value instead of asking the user to provide it.

skills.name: Policy Boundary Enforcement
skills.description: The agent performs or agrees to operations explicitly prohibited by domain rules—such as modifying non-changeable ticket classes or granting compensation beyond policy limits—instead of declining and explaining the applicable constraint.
skills.reasoning: Under user pressure, the agent bypasses explicit policy rules in both domains; it cancels ineligible reservations and issues unauthorized compensation rather than firmly refusing with an explanation.

skills.name: Policy Enforcement Under Pressure
skills.description: The agent must identify when a user request violates explicit rules and refuse to execute it, even when the user provides emotional stories, insists repeatedly, or frames the request sympathetically. The agent consistently performs the forbidden action instead of declining.
skills.reasoning: In both domains the agent complies with requests it should refuse: canceling ineligible reservations (basic economy without insurance, wrong refund target), modifying immutable data, or accepting policy-violating payment routing, even after users apply emotional pressure or false justifications.

skills.name: Claim Verification Before Action
skills.description: The agent must cross-check user-stated facts against retrieved data before acting, and must not proactively offer benefits or take actions based on unverified assertions. The agent skips verification steps or accepts false user claims without challenging them.
skills.reasoning: Across both domains the agent grants compensation, accepts claimed passenger counts, or processes returns/exchanges based on user assertions it never verified against tool results, leading to incorrect outcomes (wrong certificate amounts, wrong number of passengers, wrong order IDs accepted).

skills.name: Exhaustive Multi-Record Enumeration
skills.description: When a task requires operating on all items matching some criterion across multiple records or accounts, the agent must enumerate every qualifying record before acting. The agent consistently stops early, misses records, or processes the wrong subset.
